full_judgment:
10. In substantiating the first ground of objection, Mr. Salahuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has taken us to the recent amendment of Section 13 of the Customs Act, 1969 and argued that the National Board of Revenue pursuant to the amended provision has not yet formulated and imposed any condition, limitation and restriction on the granting of bonded warehouse licence for private warehouses and the petitioner having fulfilled all the requirements prevailing at the time, upon which the Respondent No.3 already granted licence to other competitors of the petitioner, the respondents are duty bound to grant bond licence to the petitioner on the usual terms and conditions as per prevailing practice. 

 13. Licensing of private warehouses- (1) Subject to sub-section (2) at any ware-housing station, the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board may licence private warehouses wherein dutiable goods imported by or on behalf of the licensee, or any other imported goods in respect of which facilities for deposit in a public warehouse are not available, may be deposited. (2) The Board may, from time to time, by notification in the official Gazette, impose conditions, limitations or restrictions- 

 "4. Powers and duties of officer of Customs- An officer of Customs appointed under section 3 shall exercise such powers and discharge such duties as are conferred or imposed on him by or under this Act; and he shall also be competent to exercise all powers and discharge all duties conferred or imposed upon any officer subordinate to him: Provided that, not withstanding anything contained in this Act or the rules, the Board may, by general or special order, impose such limitations or conditions on the exercise of such powers and dis-charge of such duties as it thinks fit." 

 18. We do not disagree that the customs authority in deciding the application praying for granting bonded warehouse licence is guided and control by the policy adopted by the government which may be exercised through National Board of Revenue as this provision was prevailing prior to amendment of Section 13 of Customs Act 1969. It appears that the question raised in this writ petition concerns the exercise of Power under Section 13 of the Customs Act 1969, admitting the general control of the National Board of Revenue upon the Customs authority, since a Specific power has been conferred upon the National Board of Revenue regarding imposition of control over the granting of Bonded Ware house licence by the Customs authority. But question remained whether the National Board of Revenue has yet imposed any such condition, limitation or restriction as provided by Section 13(2) of the Customs Act, 1969 and if imposed whether the National Board of Revenue has followed the mandatory procedure laid .down in the provision of law in promulgating such condition, limitation and restriction upon granting bonded Warehouse licence or that the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) is authorized to abdicate its power to the National Board of Revenue after imposition of such condition, limitation and restriction by the National Board of Revenue. 

 20. It appears from a comprehensive reading of sub-section (1) & (2) of Section 13 of the Customs Act, 1969 that National Board of Revenue is empowered to impose conditions, limitations and restrictions amongst other, on the grant of bond licence to private warehouse by the Commissioner' of Customs (Bond) in exercise of his discretionary power but the said imposition of conditions limitations and restrictions must be notified in the official gazette. On our query the learned Deputy Attorney General frankly admits that the policy formulation upon which the alleged refusal relied upon has not yet been gazette notified or no conditions, limitations, and restrictions, has yet been gazette notified, apart from only making a policy formulation dated 18.10.2003, so as to make it an exercise under the provision of sub-section (2) of Section 13 of the Customs Act, 1969. 

 22. This Annexure-C, as it appears, has 2 fold application, firstly, the Annexure-C does not impose any condition, limitation or restriction upon granting of bond licence by the Customs authority to all of or any category of industries, rather it simply explained the convenience and inconvenience of existing bond licence system concerning 18 categories of industries. Secondly it being only a letter from National Board of Revenue and not an instrument which is gazette notified, it can not achieve the status of a exercise under Section 13(2) of the Customs Act, 1969. 

 23. Therefore this Court can safely hold that the National Board of Revenue in exercise of power conferred by section 13(2) of the Customs Act, 1969 has not yet formulated and imposed any condition, limitation or restriction on the granting of bond licence to private warehouse and as such Annexure-C has no bearing upon the decision making process of the Respondent No 3 regarding grant of bond licence. Therefore the refusal to grant bonded warehouse licence relying on Annexure-C has no leg to stand and as such the same should be declared to have been made without lawful authority. 

 24. So far the question of abdication of Power by the respondent No.3 concerns, it appears that law empowered the Customs authority to exercise its discretion under Section 13(1) of the Customs Act 1969 subject to observing the condition, limitation and restriction imposed by the National Board of Revenue under the provision of Section 13(2) of the Customs Act 1969. Such a provision appears to have made the Customs authority independent from any further control by the National Board of Revenue on the matter of granting bonded ware house licence provided the National Board of Revenue has formulated and imposed such control and effected it through gazette notification. So long such specific imposition of control has not been made under the Provision of Section 13(2), the general control under Section 4 of the Customs act 1969 over the Customs authority shall be available to the National Board of Revenue as decided by their Lordships in the case of S.A. Coconut Oil Mills Limited -versus- Government of Bangladesh reported in 54 DLR 1 and accordingly the Customs authority will be bound to obtain direction form the National Board of Revenue on any question which appears to the Customs authority as discretionary exercise of power. Since we find that the National Board of Revenue has not yet formulated and imposed any condition, limitation and restriction under the Provision of Section 13(2) of Customs Act, 1969 we hold that by seeking direction in respect of granting bonded warehouse licence in fovour of the petitioner, the Respondent No.3 did not abdicate his power available un-der Section 13(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 to the Respondent No.2 National Board of Revenue rather the National Board of Revenue relying on unfounded matter directed the Respondent No.3 not to issue any further bond licence which cannot be maintained as lawful. 

 27. It further appears that Annexure C has taken into consideration the prospective Finance Act of 2003 and, aspired that the government on the basis of report of the revenue reforms committee will make control in respect of bonded warehouse licence and other related matters. From the Finance Act 2003, it appears, that the government amended the original provision of section 13 of the Customs Act, 1969 and conferred power on the National Board of Revenue to impose condition limitation and restriction upon granting of bonded warehouse licences. Therefore the aspiration as expressed in Annexure-C may be treated as has already been considered by the government and accordingly amended the provision of Customs Act. Therefore we have no hesitation to hold that refusal to grant bond licence for any industrial concern as mentioned in Annexure-H has no basis on the facts and circumstances prevailing. The customs authority since granted bonded ware-house licence to the other competitor of the petitioner and since the petitioner stands in the same footing of the other competitors, it is entitled to the grant of bond licence in relation of their imported goods including H.R. Coil.
